The emitted sequence is exactly the rule's order. EmitOpen emits the registry call, then EmitStoreFileStatus (a — the value is placed in the I-O status), then EmitUseHook. Inside the generated __IoCheckEc the body runs: `ExceptionState.SetIo(__ec!, IsFatalIoStatus(__st), ...)` when the name's checking bit is on (b — the level-3 EC-I-O condition associated with the status value, mapped by ExceptionCatalog.IoEcOfStatus per §9.1.13.1), then `__EcPerform(__ec!, __f)` consults the installed Format-3 PerformFrame FIRST (c), and only if that returns NoMatch do the F1 file-name / open-mode USE tiers and the outward GLOBAL walk run (d). §14.9.28.4 GR17's 'Any USE declarative that would normally match the exception condition is ignored' is what makes c) exclude d), and the emitter's own comment states it. PROBE (out-b1/probe/open-gr25): OPEN INPUT of an absent non-optional file with a `USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION PROCEDURE ON FN` declarative → the declarative runs and reports status 35, and the file is NOT created (a + d, and 'the file is not affected'); the same OPEN inside `PERFORM ... WHEN EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR ... END-PERFORM` → the WHEN body runs and the declarative does NOT (c), after which the run unit terminates abnormally naming EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR — which is §14.9.28.4 GR20's own tail ('If the exception condition was fatal, execution continues as specified in 14.6.13.1.3'), not a defect. CONFORMS-but-untested: no existing spec-derived test pins the OPEN-specific a-b-c-d ordering (conformance:cases/14.6.13.1.3-Fatal-exception-conditions/f3_perform_handler_turn_off_all covers the Format-3 machinery but not through an I-O statement). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED, downward to PARTIAL. The rule has a leading requirement and then four ordered actions: 'If the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful, THE FILE IS NOT AFFECTED and the following actions take place in the following order: a) ... b) ... c) ... d)'. VERIFIED HALF -- the a-b-c-d machinery is right and I could not break it. EmitOpen emits the registry call, then EmitStoreFileStatus (a), then EmitUseHook; inside __IoCheckEc the order is SetIo (b), then the F3 PerformFrame via RunTopFrame (c), then, only when no WHEN matched, the F1 file-name and open-mode USE tiers, the F3 __EcDispatch tier and the outward GLOBAL walk (d) -- which is what 14.9.49.4 GR6 requires. I also closed the leg the adjudicator left unexercised: its probe ran a FORMAT 1 USE only, but GR25 d) names 'USE FOR EXCEPTION or USE AFTER EXCEPTION', so I probed a FORMAT 3 declarative (USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR under >>TURN ... CHECKING ON) on an unsuccessful OPEN INPUT: it runs, with FS=35, EXCEPTION-STATUS=EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR and EXCEPTION-FILE=35FN. The 9.1.13.1 status->EC map in ExceptionCatalog.IoEcOfStatus matches the standard's list digit for digit. UNVERIFIED-AND-VIOLATED HALF -- 'the file is not affected'. The adjudication tested this in the only direction that cannot lose data (an absent file is not CREATED by a failing OPEN INPUT). I tested the destructive direction and it fails. Connector FA holds po.dat open INPUT under SHARING WITH NO OTHER; connector FB, a plain SELECT on the same physical file, executes OPEN OUTPUT. 9.1.13.9 1) a) and Table 19 (whose 'sharing with no other' existing column is 'Unsuccessful open' in EVERY request row) make that OPEN unsuccessful with status 61, so GR25's own consequent applies and the file shall not be affected. The compiler reports 00 and TRUNCATES po.dat to zero bytes -- the record 'KEEPTHIS01' is gone. That is wrong-answer-with-data-loss on legal source, and it is GR25's own text that is violated, not merely the detection rule's. I checked the counter-hypothesis before charging it: every unsuccessful OPEN the implementation DOES recognise leaves the file intact -- 61 on a sharing-active incoming connector returns before c.Open(mode) is ever called, 41 returns at the top of FileConnector.Open, and 35/37/30 all return before or from the failing stream construction (I confirmed 61 and 41 by probe with the content re-read intact, and the OS-level conflict variant gives 30 with the file intact). So the failure is confined to spec-unsuccessful opens the implementation misclassifies as successful, whose ROOT cause (FileRegistry.Open consults the physical-file table only when the INCOMING connector is sharing-active) is already booked DIVERGES under GR-14.9.27.4-22/-23 -- I am not re-booking that defect, I am recording that GR25's leading clause is therefore unsatisfied and was never measured. Two halves, one verified => PARTIAL by the rubric; not DIVERGES, because the four ordered actions that are the substance of the rule are correct and probed. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 for sub-rules a) and d); sub-rules b) and c) ride the exception-condition facility and the Format-3 exception-checking PERFORM, 2002 introductions, so they are adjudicated at 2002 / 2014 / 2023.
